page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. This configuration comprises 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The memory capacity is 192.0 GB, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 1843 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng tests placing both metrics in the top 25%. The AMD EPYC processor shows strong capabilities in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU encryption, and PassMark overall CPU score. Memory performance is also strong according to PassMark memory scores, though raw memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks fall within the average middle 50% range. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong performance in ray tracing and image processing, while text processing and software compilation with Clang remain in the average tier.

The instance exhibits clear performance tradeoffs when handling large language models. While text generation using a small 135M parameter model is strong, performance drops to average for medium 7B models, and text generation for large 70B models falls into the poor bottom 10% category. This makes the server less suitable for large-scale LLM inference. However, with its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, dedicated CPU allocation, and substantial local storage, the instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data compression tasks.
